items.headline: BOJ holds at 1.25% but signals December/January hike toward 1.5%
items.summary: The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at 1.25% at its Oct 29-30 meeting as universally expected, but Governor Ueda's tone and the Outlook Report point toward further hikes, with 83% of economists surveyed expecting the next move in December. A hawkish BOJ path supports continued yen strength and raises carry-trade unwind risk.
items.actionable: A hawkish BOJ hold feeds into the same global-rates narrative pressuring gold/silver today and adds a yen-strength variable for HK-tech and Asia risk sentiment at today's open.

items.headline: Gold and silver slide as hot 3.4% GDP print keeps December Fed hike alive
items.summary: Gold fell to ~$4,024-4,036/oz (-0.38%) and silver dropped ~2.5-3.45% to ~$52.13/oz on Oct 29 after a stronger-than-expected 3.4% Q3 GDP reading reinforced the case for a hawkish Fed. CME FedWatch showed ~85% probability of a December rate hike, pressuring precious metals and miners into Friday's Asia open.
items.actionable: Expect a continued soft open for the silver/gold miner sleeve (AG, HL, PAAS, GDX, SILJ, SLVP); this is a rate-driven pullback, not a change in the structural supply-deficit thesis.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00% but two hawks dissent for a hike; Warsh upgrades economy to "strong"
items.summary: The FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike -- a surprise given Cook's prior dovish lean. Chair Kevin Warsh upgraded the economy's characterization from "solid" to "strong" and pushed back on the idea AI capex is insulated from higher rates, citing widening credit spreads.
items.actionable: A genuinely hawkish hold (not a dovish pause) raises the bar for the December Fed meeting and is the proximate driver of this week's metals selloff -- watch for follow-through weakness in the miner basket.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export-control truce (expires Nov 10) has no extension in sight
items.summary: Beijing's one-year suspension of its broadest October-2025 rare-earth export controls is due to lapse Nov 10, 2026, and as of late October Beijing had published no legal notice extending it. The underlying April-2025 licensing regime for seven medium/heavy rare earths remains in force regardless.
items.actionable: The Nov 10 deadline is now 11 days out with zero signal of renewal -- the single biggest near-term catalyst for the rare-earth watchlist, and argues for staying positioned/adding into weakness in MP/Lynas/USAR ahead of the date.

items.headline: MP Materials bull case firms on DoD price-floor offtake and Apple supply deal
items.summary: With MP trading near $38 (down more than 60% from last year's ~$100 high), analysts highlight the company's government-backed offtake with a minimum price floor and guaranteed EBITDA for magnet output, plus a $500M+ multi-year supply agreement with Apple, as structural supports distinct from the rare-earth news cycle.
items.actionable: MP's downside is now partly underwritten by DoD/Apple contracts, de-risking the largest single-name position in the rare-earth watchlist heading into the Nov 10 truce deadline.

items.headline: Oil slips as Vance letter to Iran revives peace-talk hopes, offsetting Mideast risk premium
items.summary: Brent fell to ~$111.50/bbl and WTI to ~$102.82/bbl on Oct 29 as US VP JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei seeking to restart negotiations, even as President Trump separately threatened to resume strikes after the midterms. A surprise crude draw was offset by a gasoline stock build.
items.actionable: Oil's risk premium is being actively traded on diplomatic headlines in both directions -- expect continued two-way volatility in XLE/USO rather than a clean trend until the Iran-talks outcome is clearer.

items.headline: Israeli election deadlock and Netanyahu's renewed Iran-strike threats raise Gulf alarm
items.summary: Israel's election produced no clear majority; opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot urged the military to resist post-election pressure from PM Netanyahu, who has threatened new strikes on Iran. The US separately warned Gulf states of a possible renewed Iranian offensive after next week's US midterm elections.
items.actionable: Political instability in Israel plus a live Iran-strike threat keeps a geopolitical floor under oil and a safe-haven bid under gold even as rate-driven selling dominates today -- don't read the metals dip as risk-off abating.

items.headline: NYT: Jensen Huang reportedly cultivated by suspected Chinese intelligence asset tied to Nvidia customer Megaspeed
items.summary: The New York Times reported US officials believe an executive at Singapore-linked cloud firm Megaspeed developed a close relationship with Nvidia's CEO to pass intelligence to Beijing; Commerce had been probing Megaspeed's Malaysian data center since 2024 over undeployed Nvidia chips. Nvidia disputed the report's chip-diversion characterization, calling it "investigated and debunked."
items.actionable: Renewed scrutiny of Nvidia-to-China chip diversion raises the odds of tighter enforcement, a tailwind for the China domestic-substitution narrative underpinning SMIC even as it adds headline risk to the broader AI-chip trade.

items.headline: Tencent and Visa sign MoU on cross-border payments and agentic AI commerce
items.summary: Tencent and Visa announced a broadened partnership covering cross-border payments (TenPay Global/Visa Pay), Visa Direct transfers into Weixin Pay, and agentic-commerce AI-shopping experiments, following Chinese regulatory approvals for deeper payments cooperation. Tencent shares dipped on the day despite the announcement.
items.actionable: A positive medium-term monetization signal for Tencent's fintech/AI-commerce stack, but it did not move the stock up on the day -- not an immediate catalyst to act on.

items.headline: Keppel REIT drops 4.85% on S$611-626M Keppel South Central acquisition from sponsor
items.summary: Keppel REIT agreed to buy a 51% stake in Keppel South Central (Tanjong Pagar office tower, ~60% pre-leased) from parent Keppel Ltd for roughly S$611-626M, part of Keppel's S$3.7B asset-monetization program this year. Units fell 4.85% on announcement-day dilution/funding concerns even as OCBC Research reiterated a Buy with a S$0.93 fair value on 22% projected income growth.
items.actionable: The sell-the-news reaction looks like near-term equity/placement-overhang risk rather than a thesis change -- OCBC's unchanged Buy call suggests weakness could be a tactical add opportunity.

items.headline: Singapore banks still digesting early-October selloff ahead of Q3 results (DBS Nov 5, OCBC Nov 6)
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB fell 6-10% in early October on a bond-yield surge and a Citi downgrade of OCBC to Sell over SORA-driven margin compression; shares remain pressured heading into Q3 results. OCBC Research issued fresh Oct 29 SG-REIT calls: Buy on CapitaLand India Trust and Keppel REIT, Hold on First REIT and Mapletree Industrial Trust.
items.actionable: The bank sleeve is trading on bond-yield/NIM fears into early-November earnings -- size any dip-buying with the Nov 5/6 results dates in mind rather than reacting to today's price action alone.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides below $80K as Alphabet earnings miss and Samsung weakness hit tech sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin fell toward $78,690-80,727 on Oct 29/30, down from a post-Fed bounce above $81,700, as disappointing Alphabet results and weak Samsung chip guidance weighed on risk sentiment broadly. US spot Bitcoin ETFs nonetheless logged a third straight day of inflows ($137.3M on Wednesday).
items.actionable: Crypto weakness is tracking the same tech-earnings/rate-driven risk-off hitting metals and HK tech this week -- a read-through confirming broad risk aversion rather than a crypto-specific issue.

items.headline: KOSPI explodes +6.63% to a record on SK Hynix blowout AI-memory earnings and $75B buyback
items.summary: SK Hynix reported an 80% operating margin on record Q3 earnings and pledged an 80-100 trillion won (~$75B) buyback, sending Samsung +9% and triggering a buy-side circuit breaker on the KOSPI. Foreign investors bought a net ~₩1.15 trillion, the largest single-day foreign net buy in 51 days.
items.actionable: Confirms the AI-memory supercycle thesis underpinning SMH/semis exposure, though Thursday's -1.24% pullback on Samsung's capital-return disappointment shows the move is fragile, not a clean trend.

items.headline: Newmont posts record Q3 adjusted profit on gold strength and Cadia copper recovery
items.summary: Newmont reported record Q3 adjusted net income of $2.3B ($2.20/share), with revenue up 15% YoY to $6.36B and EBITDA near $4B, beating estimates. Copper output at the Cadia mine jumped 35% quarter-on-quarter and the company ended the quarter with a $3.2B net cash position.
items.actionable: NEM's balance-sheet strength and cost discipline make it the most defensive name in the miner sleeve to lean on if the Fed/BOJ-driven metals pullback extends.
